clue.text: Swindle foreign wife and daughter

parts.note: Frau is the German word for a wife

explanation.surface: Someone cheats a wife from abroad and her daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle is a con or deception, the same thing as a piece of trickery.

clue.text: Like the US, defeat Red combination

indicators.note: a combination mixes things together, so the letters of the two words are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: An American victory over the Reds, achieved by teamwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combination' rearranges DEFEATRED, the letters of 'defeat' and 'Red' together.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States is a union of member states under a central government, a federal arrangement.

clue.text: Inclined to use a canvas covering

parts.note: a tilt is an old word for a canvas awning or the cloth hood of a cart

explanation.surface: Someone tends to favour a tarpaulin over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to use' is only a link. TILT as a cloth cover is an old sense, as on a cart or stall.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tipped at an angle, slanting, is leaning over.

clue.text: May dread changing ends — fancy that!

indicators.note: changing here means the outer letter at the start of the phrase is switched for the one at its end
the ends of the phrase are its first and last letters, which trade places with each other

explanation.surface: A girl called May fears something will be altered, and the clue exclaims at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing ends' swaps the M at the start of 'May dread' with the D at its end, turning MAYDREAD into DAYDREAM; 'that!' finishes the exclamation 'fancy that!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverie or flight of imagination is a fantasy, one meaning of the noun fancy.

clue.text: Turn suddenly to make a collection

definitions.meaning: to spin about sharply on the spot
money gathered informally from a group, say for a colleague's leaving present

explanation.surface: Someone spins on their heel to pass the hat around.
explanation.definitionFit: Whipping round is wheeling sharply; a whip-round is an informal office fund-raising for a gift.

clue.text: River Don

definitions.meaning: the ... flows through Durham in north-east England
to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: Names a river called the Don.
explanation.walkthrough: The Don is itself a river, which is the trap; here 'Don' is the verb for putting on clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wear is a river in County Durham, England; to put on clothing is to have it on your body.

clue.text: Use dingo in cooking for aboriginal

indicators.note: something being cooked is being worked over, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe suggesting the wild dog be used in the pot as native food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in cooking' rearranges the letters of 'Use dingo'; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboriginal and indigenous both describe peoples or species native to a place from earliest times.

clue.text: Put in novel situation, deliver speech in audition

indicators.note: audition is literally hearing, so the word is identified by how it sounds

parts.note: to recite is to say a speech or poem aloud from memory

explanation.surface: An actor gives a speech at an audition in a new setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audition' suggests a theatre tryout, but it means hearing: RECITE, spoken, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To place something in a new location is to relocate it to a fresh site.

clue.text: Mutual arrangement about boy's final demand

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the anagram goes around the name
an arrangement puts things in a new order, so the letters of the word are reordered

parts.note: Tim is a boy's name; the possessive adds nothing

explanation.surface: A deal both sides agreed on regarding the lad's last request.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' gives the anagram ULATUM, which 'about' wraps around the boy's name to make UL-TIM-ATUM.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultimatum is a last set of terms, backed by a threat if refused.

clue.text: Way in which name's entered as benefactor

indicators.note: name is entered, meaning placed inside the doorway word

parts.note: a door is an entrance

explanation.surface: A building entrance where a sponsor's name is inscribed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which' and 'as' are link words; 'name's entered' reads as 'name is entered', putting N into DOOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor gives money or goods to a cause, as any benefactor does.

clue.text: Farm-worker many turned to help

indicators.note: turned means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a myriad is a countless number, a great many
aid is help

explanation.surface: A lot of people switched over to assisting on the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses MYRIAD to DAIRYM; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairymaid was a woman employed to milk cows and make butter on a farm.

clue.text: Demonstrated smooth fabric

definitions.meaning: to sit in is to protest by occupying a place

explanation.surface: Someone showed off a sleek cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demonstrated' looks like 'showed'; read it as protested, split SAT IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Protesters sat in, occupying a building; satin is a glossy silk-like cloth.

clue.text: Come back with laboratory apparatus

definitions.meaning: a glass vessel with a long bent neck used for distilling

explanation.surface: Someone returns carrying chemistry kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp riposte answers someone; a distilling flask with a downturned neck carries the same name.

clue.text: Urge to send back this puzzle, perhaps? Only for a Provost of Eton

definitions.text: this puzzle, perhaps? Only for a Provost of Eton

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to remit is to send money

explanation.surface: A temptation to return the crossword, which only a famous headmaster could finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; 'back' reverses REMIT. The definition recalls a Provost of Eton who supposedly finished The Times crossword while his breakfast egg boiled, so the puzzle timed his egg.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sandglass measuring boiling time; the puzzle served the Provost as one.

clue.text: Chocolate biscuit from Italian city

definitions.meaning: a thin crisp biscuit of nuts and fruit coated on one side with chocolate
describing something or someone from Florence

explanation.surface: A chocolate treat imported from Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The biscuit named after Florence is nut and fruit with chocolate; the adjective means of that Tuscan city.

clue.text: Sail to pierhead with escort

parts.note: split as 'pier head': the head, or first letter, of the word pier
a gallant is a man escorting a lady

explanation.surface: Someone sails to the end of the pier with a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pierhead' is a real word but here splits as 'pier head', the first letter of pier; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: On a square-rigged ship, the sail set above the topsail is one of its named sails.

clue.text: Fish with rod — what could be plainer?

parts.note: a pike is a predatory freshwater fish
a staff is a stick or rod

explanation.surface: An angler with a fishing rod, and nothing could be simpler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. The definition rests on the idiom 'as plain as a pikestaff', meaning perfectly obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'plain as a pikestaff' makes the spear shaft the standard of plainness.

clue.text: Naturally you won't find oysters in this dish

definitions.text: Naturally you won't find oysters in this dish

parts.words: Naturally you won't find oysters in this dish
parts.note: a hotchpotch dish, but also an old word for an artificial pond where fish or oysters are kept, so oysters there are not natural

explanation.surface: A cook notes that shellfish do not normally go into this meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a recipe without shellfish; the joke is that an oyster bed or fish pond is also called a stew, and oysters in one are farmed, not found naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: A slowly simmered dish of meat and vegetables; also an old name for a fish or oyster pond.

clue.text: Affected by moving air, some musicians sobbed

parts.note: the winds are the wind players of an orchestra
wept means cried, sobbed

explanation.surface: Some orchestra players cried in a draughty hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A place exposed to gales is blown about by them.

clue.text: Endlessly recommend swallowing a liqueur

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to advocate a course is to recommend it

explanation.surface: Someone keeps suggesting you drink a liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' trims ADVOCATE to ADVOCAT, and 'swallowing' puts A inside it: ADVOCA-A-T.
explanation.definitionFit: Advocaat is a Dutch egg-and-brandy drink, a sweet liqueur.

clue.text: Noble expected to defend monarch

indicators.note: defending means surrounding and shielding, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: due means expected, as a train is due
K is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An aristocrat is expected to protect the sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to defend' puts DUE around K.
explanation.definitionFit: A duke is the highest rank of the British peerage.

clue.text: Instructs soldier, one who prepares for pitched battle

definitions.text: one who prepares for pitched battle

parts.note: to ground someone in a subject is to teach them its basics
a man is a soldier of the ranks

explanation.surface: Orders a trooper; someone readies for a fierce fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitched battle' suggests warfare, but means a sports contest on a pitch, prepared by this groundkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: The groundkeeper rolls and marks the pitch before a cricket or football match.

clue.text: Financial agent bankrupted king

parts.note: broke means having no money, bankrupt
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A money-man ruined the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockbroker buys and sells shares for clients, as an agent in finance.

clue.text: Tit for tat, for example, in race on motorway

indicators.note: on means following in this across clue, so the race comes after the motorway

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI
a sprint is a short fast race

explanation.surface: Retaliation in a road race on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. The M1 runs London to Leeds; crosswords read the digit as I. Tit for tat could be a misprint of 'tat for tat' or similar.
explanation.definitionFit: A typo, an error in printed text, is what a garbled phrase could be.

clue.text: Was contemplating showing doctor around practice

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: MD is Doctor of Medicine
use is practice, as in custom and usage

explanation.surface: Was thinking while seeing a GP about his surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing' is a link; the doctor goes around practice, so the container gives M-USE-D.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to ponder or think deeply.

clue.text: Collected writings in part of Oxford or Cambridge college

definitions.meaning: the whole body of a writer's works

definitions.text: part of Oxford or Cambridge college
definitions.meaning: ... Christi is the name of a college at both Oxford and Cambridge

explanation.surface: Anthologies kept in an Oxbridge college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of texts by an author is a complete set; Corpus Christi is a college at both Oxford and Cambridge.

clue.text: Good time one had in 1993, for example

definitions.meaning: the best period of life, as in 'in her heyday'
1993 is divisible only by itself and 1

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a great time back in 1993.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' links the two definitions; 1993 looks like a date but is a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Your heyday is the peak of life; a number with no divisors but itself and one is called this.

clue.text: Attend to switch

definitions.meaning: informally, to deal with someone by thrashing them
to whip with a thin cane or switch

explanation.surface: An order to look after the changeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch' looks like a change; here it is the verb to whip, and 'attend to' is the threatening sense of dealing with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitting repeatedly is thrashing; to switch someone is to lash them with a cane, and to 'see to' someone can mean the same.

clue.text: Boat's distinctive smell

definitions.meaning: a small sailing vessel used for fishing

explanation.surface: A vessel's peculiar odour.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-masted fishing vessel carries this name; a smack is also a flavour or hint of something.

clue.text: One special treat I have over and over again

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: special as in specially prepared, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A single special treat that I keep having repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' rearranges TREAT to TERAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repeated over and over is repetitive, done in cycles.

clue.text: Holding back of French excitement

parts.note: de is French for of
a ferment is a state of agitation or excitement

explanation.surface: The restraint of French enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Postponement, putting off a call-up or payment, is a kind of delay.

clue.text: Lifting paper with leading article

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so the article comes before the paper

parts.note: the is the definite article
FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: Picking up a newspaper with its front-page story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. 'Lifting' looks like raising, but is slang for stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something is slang for stealing it, so lifting is stealing.
